messages:
maria: FYI - noticed a p99 bump (~25%) on llm-13b chat after the runtime kernel selector change this morning. metrics -> https://dashboards/reports/xyz (short summary below).

jon: which selector change? kernel ranking or the fallback threshold?

maria: we switched to prefer the new fused-attn path for short sequences, but metrics show increased CPU in the path that handles KV-cache invalidations. sequence distribution shifted (more tiny prefix-heavy chats).

akshay: ran a quick perf sample. flamegraph shows a big spike in matmul_generic when kv hits occur. looks like kernel selector is choosing non-quantized fallback because effective head_dim != expected layout after RMSNorm/SiLU path change. snippet:

```
Profile samples breakdown (sampling):
  42% matmul_kernel_generic
  18% kv_cache_serialize
  10% optimized_gemm_fused
  8% attention_rotary_apply
  6% rmsnorm_forward
```

jon: hmm. any config diffs between model variants? Llama-3 configs we onboarded had head_dim = 128 vs 96 for old builds. if head_dim changes, some kernels don't trigger the packed GEMM fastpath.

maria: yes - model-catalog changed hidden dim -> 5120, heads -> 40 (head_dim=128). previous was 4096 / 32 (128 too but precomp/layouts were different because rope_theta defaults changed). also we changed rope_theta default from 10_000 -> 8192 in the catalog to match community weights. that affects rotary frequency and our RoPE scaling micro-ops.

sophie: the batching heuristic is also part of this. we currently flush after 8ms or when batch size >= 16. for short chat bursts most requests are 1-3 tokens and we wait the timeout which causes many small batches with different seq_len leading to kernel churn. two ideas: (1) adaptive timeout based on recent seq_len histogram, (2) group by (model_variant, head_dim, rope_theta_bucket) before selecting kernel.

akshay: did a repro where I force rope_theta=10000 at runtime and bump batch timeout to 3ms. result: p99 dropped ~18% and matmul_generic time decreased. command I used to repro:

```
# local harness
./run_perf --model llm-13b --override '{"rope_theta":10000, "batching": {"max_wait_ms": 3}}' --qps 200 --seq_dist 'short_chat'
```

jon: interesting — suggests two interacting regressions: kernel-selection heuristics not grouping by effective RoPE layout, and batching policy causing unstable batch composition.

maria: also noticed KV cache behavior: we invalidate entire prefix on certain chat-template branches because the template rewrite inserts a hidden system token at start. that triggers KV reserialize which is expensive. small change: treat those template-only edits as metadata, don't evict cache. easy fix in the chat-template applier.

sophie: actionable plan: (A) add head_dim + rope_theta bucket to kernel selector key, (B) make batching adaptive: for models with >70% short seqs reduce wait to 3ms, (C) change chat-template applier to avoid physical KV rewrite for system-only edits. seems safe for canary.

maria: +1 on plan. will open a PR for chat-template change.

akshay: I'll prototype the selector key change and run A/B on the dedicated pool tonight. will post perf diffs.

perf-bot: Canary job queued: canary/dedicated/llm-13b -> overrides {rope_theta:10000, batching.max_wait_ms:3} (triggered by akshay). :white_check_mark:

jon: thanks. if akshay's selector patch looks good let's roll to prod with a fallback flag in case quantized kernels misdetect layout. :thumbsup:

maria: leaving this thread with the short repro and the profiling snippet above. ping me if you need env or the exact traces. :mag:
